body.cap: GEOGRID’s smart water purification system ‘BLOS’ on display | Photo by AVING News

body.x: South Korean startup GEOGRID, a partner of the Ministry of Environment and K-water, showcased its smart water purification system ‘BLOS (Building Oasis)’ for the first time at CES 2025, held in Las Vegas from January 7 to 10 (local time).

Located in Eureka Park, the startup exhibition section of CES, GEOGRID’s booth attracted significant attention throughout the event. The Small Business Administration (SBA) recognized BLOS’ innovative water quality management solution as a prime example of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) management, impressing visitors and representatives from global corporations.

BLOS is a system that cleans and maintains the interior of water pipes using ionization and artificial intelligence (AI) technology without replacing existing pipelines. This technology removes impurities from water and enables real-time AI-based water quality monitoring and predictive analysis to detect issues in advance.

Its eco-friendly ion sterilization method eliminates chemicals, reduces reliance on plastic bottled water and conventional water purifiers, and reduces carbon emissions. This dual benefit of environmental protection and economic efficiency has made BLOS an attractive business solution. A European hotel chain executive who visited the booth remarked, “BLOS perfectly aligns with our ESG goals.”

GEOGRID CEO Kihyun Kim stated, “BLOS is not just about providing clean water; it is a sustainable technology that considers both the environment and people. We are delighted to introduce BLOS’s value to global partners at CES 2025.”

Co-founder James Jeong highlighted, “In the U.S., managing old building pipelines is a significant challenge. Conventional solutions often rely on chemicals like PFAS or only provide temporary prevention. However, alternative technologies are needed with stricter environmental regulations and growing health concerns.” He added, “BLOS integrates permanent ionization technology with AI to maintain clean pipelines without relying on PFAS, offering an eco-friendly solution that sets a new standard in the water quality management industry.”

body.cap: GEOGRID’s booth at CES 2025. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Overseas Business Manager Sangmi Oh commented, “BLOS is being recognized as an alternative technology that surpasses the limitations of existing water purification systems while meeting environmental regulations and carbon reduction demands. At CES, we engaged in business meetings with key facility operators from hotels, hospitals, and schools, actively discussing initial export opportunities and receiving positive feedback on potential partnerships.”

Through CES 2025, GEOGRID demonstrated BLOS’s excellence on the global stage and introduced a new paradigm in water quality management. It merged environmental, technological, and economic innovations to reshape the global water purification market.

Recently, GEOGRID was selected for the Ministry of SMEs and Startups’ TIPS R&D program, further validating its technological capabilities and growth potential. With this support, the company is accelerating research and development of the BLOS system and expanding into global markets.

CEO Kihyun Kim stated, “Being selected for the TIPS R&D program is a significant milestone proving BLOS’s technological excellence and global competitiveness. We leverage this opportunity to expand our business into the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, establishing ourselves as a global leader in ESG-driven innovation.”
AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, plans to launch several programs to boost the global reach of Korean SMEs and startups.

They will set up the AVING BROADCASTING ZONE at the Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, host the CES Media Day Startup Conference, and organize global media interviews to share Korean startup news worldwide. International media reporters affiliated with Aving News will cover all programs.

After CES 2025, AVING News will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea to enhance corporate visibility. Before CES, they will also share key CES participation strategies with domestic SMEs and startups, invite two global media outlets for pre-event interviews, and arrange online interviews between startups and overseas media representatives.
